newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Codelco sees Asian copper demand up 19 pct by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Codelco sees Asian copper demand up 19 pct by 2000.

text.p: Asian copper consumption is forecast to jump by over 19 percent to five million tonnes by 2000, powered mainly by explosive growth in the infrastructure and energy sectors, a senior Codelco official said on Monday.

"Refined copper consumption in Asia has increased substantially," said Luis Miqueles, managing director of Codelco Asia, the Singapore-based arm of the Chilean state copper giant, at a copper conference here.

"From 1992 to 1996, consumption grew from 3.3 million tonnes to more than 4.2 million tonnes. We forecast that by the year 2000, Asian refined copper consumption could reach above five million tonnes," he said.

The low comparative level of infrastructure and increasing levels of energy consumption will fuel Asian demand, with most of it coming from China and the "tiger economies" of Southeast Asia, Miqueles said.
Asian copper imports are estimated to have reached around 1.4 million tonnes in 1996 and may reach 1.7 million tonnes by the end of the decade.
Some of the deficit can be covered by new projects that may come on stream over the next few years.
"There will be projects and some of them will be a reality," Miqueles said.

Codelco is the world's largest copper miner and accounted for 14 percent of western world mined copper in 1996. Its share of western production is seen rising to around 15 percent by 2000 or 2001, company officials said.
